data.description:

data.title: SK Hynix Could Raise $15B in Solidigm IPO at $150B Valuation
data.description:
Memory chipmaker SK Hynix (SKHY) is considering a U.S. IPO for its Solidigm storage business as soon as 2027 in a deal that could raise about $15 billion and value the company at $150 billion. According to Reuters, Solidigm has started talks with potential advisers as SK Hynix considers listing the business separately. A deal at that size would put Solidigm among the largest semiconductor IPOs ever in the U.S.

Solidigm became part of SK Hynix after the company bought Intel's (INTC) NAND flash memory business in 2021 and renamed it. Since then, Solidigm has focused heavily on storage products for large data centers. Its enterprise solid-state drives can hold as much as 122 terabytes in a device roughly the size of a pack of cards.

That business has become more important as AI systems require huge amounts of storage alongside GPUs and other computing equipment.

As a result, Solidigm has started signing deals that tie its growth more directly to the AI infrastructure buildout.

Solidigm Is Becoming More Important to AI Data Centers

Indeed, in August, Solidigm signed a multi-year agreement with AI cloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) that gives CoreWeave priority access to enterprise SSD capacity. That storage will support CoreWeave's AI cloud platform as customer workloads grow. CoreWeave said that AI systems depend on storage working closely with computing and networking hardware.

This helps explain why Solidigm could command such a large valuation. The company is no longer simply selling storage for traditional data centers. Its products are increasingly tied to the infrastructure needed to run AI workloads. Solidigm also works with customers such as Dell Technologies (DELL) and data platform company Vast Data.

An IPO would give investors a separate way to invest in part of SK Hynix's NAND storage business if they choose to specifically target that part of its operations.

The company is based in Rancho Cordova, California, and has more than 2,000 employees. It operates from 13 locations globally.

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Holds Firm Despite Volatile Trading Week
data.description:
Bitcoin's (BTC) price has held firm despite a volatile trading week for cryptocurrencies. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization was trading at $64,000 in mid-afternoon trading on Sept. 24 and headed for a winning week despite suffering several knocks in recent days. Digital assets, like stocks, have been under pressure as yields U.S. Treasury yields have surged in recent days.

But while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average has declined over four consecutive weeks, Bitcoin has managed to continue rally that began at the end of August. BTC is up 3% on the week and continues a win streak that began a month ago and has taken Bitcoin's price 30% higher. Other cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE) also continue to move upwards.

Stocks and cryptocurrencies are getting some relief at week's end as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury holds firm at 5.175% after steadily climbing in recent days.

data.title: Lawmakers Cry Foul as Polymarket Allows Bets on U.S. Bank Failures
data.description:
Lawmakers in Washington, D.C. are crying foul after Polymarket announced that it will allow some users of its prediction market platform to bet on bank failures in the United States. Regulators and lawmakers have been quick to raise concerns over bets against the American financial system. For its part, Polymarket says that the bets on bank failures are a small part of its offshore platform, and Americans user are banned from placing such bets.

Still, regulators and lawmakers say they are worried whether such betting could grow in volume and fuel a bank run at leading institutions such as JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Bank of America (BAC), and Citigroup (C). Prediction markets allow users to bet on the outcomes of real-world events such as sports and elections. However, they also allow people to bet on the weather and if airplanes will land at their scheduled time.

America's Financial Health

Federal Deposit Insurance officials in the U.S. have questioned whether there was any legitimate commercial or investment benefit to betting on the failure of American banks, and whether the agency's internal ethics restrictions were strong enough to prohibit insiders from trading on the platforms. News of the betting on bank failures comes a precarious time for the U.S. economy.

Earlier in September, the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, ratcheting up borrowing costs for consumers and businesses. At the same time, the U.S. national debt recently surpassed $40 trillion and yields on U.S. Treasurys have risen to their highest levels in 20 years as demand for government bonds weakens.

Multiple Lawsuits Against Polymarket

News that Polymarket is allowing people to bet on whether U.S. banks will fail comes days after the prediction market was hit the latest in a series of lawsuits. New York has become the latest U.S. state to sue Polymarket and try to block it from operating in its jurisdiction. New York is accusing the prediction market of operating an illegal gambling operation and has asked a court to prevent it from operating within the state.

Other U.S. states, including Massachusetts and Rhode Island, have taken similar legal action against Polymarket this year. A dispute is underway over whether prediction markets should be regulated by U.S. states or the federal government. Traditionally, gaming has fallen under state control. New York prosecutors argue that Polymarket's contracts meet the state's definition of gambling and therefore require a license from the New York State Gaming Commission.

Polymarket is a private company and its stock doesn't trade on a public exchange.

data.title: On Holding Stock Gets Sell Rating as Jefferies Calls 2029 Goals Too Ambitious
data.description:
Premium athletic brand On Holding (ONON) has rallied by 12% over four sessions after setting ambitious 2029 targets. Nevertheless, Jefferies still sees major downside. Indeed, analyst Randal Konik kept his Sell rating and $20 price target. Konik believes that On remains a niche brand and may struggle to reach its goal of 5.6 billion Swiss francs in annual sales by 2029. That concern starts with On's recent growth in the Americas, one of its most important markets.

Second-quarter sales in the region grew by just 4.5% and missed analyst expectations. Therefore, On would need sales growth to speed up significantly over the next few years to reach its 2029 target.

Jefferies questions whether that can happen because On remains focused on premium products. The average price of its shoes has increased to about $170 from $145 five years ago.

Jefferies Thinks On's Market May Be Too Limited

Konik argues that On does not have the same reach as larger competitors such as Nike (NKE) and Adidas (ADDYY). Those companies sell products at many price points and have long histories in both sports and fashion. On has a narrower product range, which Jefferies believes could make its long-term growth targets harder to reach.

On is trying to change that by entering new sports. The company recently signed football (soccer) star Kylian Mbappe and plans to launch golf products in 2027.

However, Konik believes that building credibility in new sports will take time because On does not have a long history in those categories.

data.title: Intel's (INTC) Comeback Is Real. Is the Market Ready to Believe It?
data.description:
Intel (INTC), the once-beloved computer chip manufacturer, is making a comeback, and its numbers back it up. Even though it has suffered over the last four years with falling revenue, compressing margins, and mounting losses, it's hard to ignore that the company posted Q2 2026 numbers in July that beat across nearly every metric. Wall Street may still rate Intel a firm "Hold," but investors who don't act now are likely to pay a premium on today's stock price later. Intel looks like a Buy, and the case for getting into the stock now is stronger than cautious analyst ratings suggest.

Supporting the Buy case is that Intel has spent the last four years absorbing a decline that would have broken lesser companies. Revenue fell from $79 billion in 2021 to $52.8 billion last year. Earnings swung from $4.89 per share to deep losses, while gross margins compressed steadily from above 45% to under 39%.

While Intel might be the exact definition of what happens when a dominant technology name misses a cycle and changing consumer habits, this story is now changing for the better. Its entry into artificial intelligence (AI) is going to help turn the once-giant chip manufacturer into the next computing giant.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Advances as U.S.-Iran Talks Progress; Trumps Hails 'Productive Meeting' With Xi Jinping
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is up 0.79% on Friday amid lower oil prices and as the Trump-Xi summit comes to a conclusion. Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is down 2.9% to $103.45 per barrel following news that U.S. and Iranian negotiators at the United Nations General Assembly had discussed a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The talks have progressed and entered into a more detailed and technical phase, sources told Al Jazeera.

However, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains limited. Nine vessels passed through the global oil chokepoint on Thursday, down from 14 on Wednesday and below the 10-day average of 18. Since the start of the war on February 28, Brent has climbed 33%, while average gas prices in the U.S. are up 51%.

Elsewhere, President Trump described his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as "productive," adding that "tremendous things will be happening." Earlier this week, the two countries agreed to extend their trade truce to January 10, 2027. Furthermore, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the two world powers had reached a trade agreement covering certain U.S. agricultural products, medical devices, non-sensitive Chinese consumer goods, and more.

data.title: T-Mobile (TMUS) Raises Quarterly Dividend by 15%
data.description:
Telecommunications giant T-Mobile (TMUS) has raised its quarterly dividend by 15%. T-Mobile has declared a dividend of $1.17 per, up 15% from its previous distribution of $1.02. The new dividend gives TMUS stock a forward yield 2.83%. The next dividend from the company is payable on Dec. 10 to shareholders of record as of Nov. 25.

T-Mobile initiated its first-ever quarterly dividend in December 2023 and has raised it for three consecutive years. News of the dividend has given TMUS stock a modest lift on Sept. 25. However, the company's share price has declined 30% over the last 12 months amid rising competition in the market for wireless internet and telecommunications services.
